run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend since 2026-11-16T16:09:07Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate warning for otel-demo/frontend is backed by real frontend error spans, and every one of them sits on the checkout call path. frontend's POST /api/checkout spans and its client span grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder started returning STATUS_CODE_ERROR at ~16:08-16:09 (first non-zero 5m-rate sample at 16:09:07, rising to ~0.75 errors/s), while its other operations (GET /api/cart, GET /api/data, GET /api/products/{productId}, GET /api/recommendations, POST /api/cart, Cart/GetCart, Cart/AddItem, AdService/GetAds, ProductCatalogService/GetProduct, RecommendationService/ListRecommendations) show zero error spans. The dependency behind that call, checkout pod checkout-5dccddf8bb-9dn2q, is in CrashLoopBackOff: its container 'checkout' has 11 restarts, last termination reason Error with exit code 2 at 16:15:00, no ready container, and the deployment 'checkout' consequently reports 1 desired replica but no ready/available replicas, with the checkout Service endpoint listing only notReadyAddresses. checkout's own span throughput fell from ~8.4 spans/s at 16:09:07 to 0 from 16:15:07 on. The pod's container image and its wait-for-kafka init image are both gcr.io/google-containers/pause:latest, while the pod carries annotations recording the original images (checkout-normal=ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-checkout, wait-for-kafka-init=busybox:latest); the Deployment and ReplicaSet templates still specify the correct images, and kubelet events show 'Container checkout definition changed, will be restarted' 7 times from 16:08:00 plus BackOff warnings from 16:10:00. This pod is the only pod in the namespace with a pause image. So the alert is a downstream symptom: the frontend fails only on PlaceOrder because its sole checkout backend was replaced by a non-serving pause container and is crash-looping.

claims.text: frontend emitted error spans during the incident: sum(rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="frontend",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}[5m])) was 0.248 span-errors/s at 2026-11-16T16:09:07Z.

The frontend errors are confined to the checkout path: error rates became non-zero at 16:09:07 only for span_name POST /api/checkout, POST, executing api route (pages) /api/checkout, grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder and tcp.connect (peak ~0.748/s, ~0.748/s, ~0.748/s, ~0.748/s and ~0.056/s), while GET /api/cart, POST /api/cart, GET /api/data, grpc.oteldemo.CartService/GetCart, grpc.oteldemo.CartService/AddItem and grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds error rates stayed 0 across the window.

Across all services with error-labelled span series in the window, the elevated error rates were on frontend (POST /api/checkout and CheckoutService/PlaceOrder ~0.748/s) and frontend-proxy (ingress ~0.767/s, router frontend egress ~0.756/s); accounting, payment, ad and recommendation error series were 0 apart from small pre-existing flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream errors (~0.004/s, present before 16:08 and unrelated to the checkout failures), and service checkout itself had no error spans.

Pod checkout-5dccddf8bb-9dn2q (owner ReplicaSet checkout-5dccddf8bb) is Running but not ready: container checkout ready=false, restartCount=11, lastState terminated reason=Error exitCode=2 finishedAt 2026-11-16T16:15:00Z; all other 20 pods in otel-demo had ready containers and restartCount 0.

The checkout container is in state waiting/CrashLoopBackOff ("back-off 2m40s restarting failed container=checkout") and the pod's Ready and ContainersReady conditions are False with reason ContainersNotReady since 2026-11-16T16:15:00Z.

Deployment checkout has DESIRED=1 but READY and AVAILABLE are unset (no ready replicas), and ReplicaSet checkout-5dccddf8bb reports replicas=1 with readyReplicas unset; every other deployment in otel-demo reported READY=1 and AVAILABLE=1.
The checkout Service endpoint contains only notReadyAddresses: pod checkout-5dccddf8bb-9dn2q (IP 100.96.4.26) on port tcp-service/8080, i.e. no ready backend for frontend's PlaceOrder calls.

checkout stopped serving: sum(rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="checkout"}[5m])) fell from 8.393 spans/s at 16:09:07 to 4.6 at 16:11:07, 1.268 at 16:13:07, and 0 from 16:15:07 through 16:24:07.

The pod's live spec no longer runs the checkout application: container 'checkout' has image gcr.io/google-containers/pause:latest and initContainer 'wait-for-kafka' also has image gcr.io/google-containers/pause:latest, while the pod's annotations record the original images as checkout-normal=ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-checkout and wait-for-kafka-init=busybox:latest.

Kubelet events for checkout-5dccddf8bb-9dn2q show 7x Normal/Killing "Container checkout definition changed, will be restarted" between 16:08:00Z and 16:11:00Z, 6x Normal/Pulled of image gcr.io/google-containers/pause:latest between 16:08:00Z and 16:14:27Z, and 26x Warning/BackOff "Back-off restarting failed container checkout" between 16:10:00Z and 16:15:48Z.

The owner workload templates are unchanged and still correct: Deployment checkout's pod template uses image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-checkout with initContainer wait-for-kafka (busybox:latest), and ReplicaSet checkout-5dccddf8bb (owner Deployment checkout) uses image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-checkout.

Only one pod in otel-demo carries a pause image and image-override annotations: checkout-5dccddf8bb-9dn2q (images gcr.io/google-containers/pause:latest x2, ready=false, annotations checkout-normal and wait-for-kafka-init). All other pods ran their normal images (e.g. frontend-675fd7b5c5-gc9hg = ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-frontend, frontend-proxy = ...2.1.3-frontend-proxy, payment = ...2.1.3-payment) with no such annotations.

Before the crash loop, the checkout container's retrievable log stream shows a healthy order flow ("[PlaceOrder]", "payment went through", "order placed", "order confirmation email sent", "Successful to write message") with the last readable line at 2026-11-16T15:54:09Z; the previous container instance's logs were unavailable (HTTP 400: previous terminated container not found).

Measured frontend error-span share at the alert instant was 0.455% (error span rate / total span rate * 100 at 2026-11-16T16:09:07Z), which does not reproduce the alert annotation's value 3.5; the alert rule's own expression could not be retrieved.

frontend itself is not the faulty component at container level: pod frontend-675fd7b5c5-gc9hg is Running and ready with restartCount 0 and runs image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-frontend, and its non-checkout operations had zero error spans.

Rejected: the checkout container was OOMKilled or resource-starved. Its last termination reason is Error with exitCode 2 (not OOMKilled) after ~5s of runtime (startedAt 16:14:55, finishedAt 16:15:00), and the container image in the pod is the pause image, not the checkout app.

Rejected: this was a controller-driven rollout or reschedule of checkout. No SuccessfulDelete/SuccessfulCreate events appear; the pod name, ReplicaSet owner checkout-5dccddf8bb and startTime 2026-11-16T15:31:18Z are unchanged, deletionTimestamp is null, and the observed events are in-place 'Container checkout definition changed, will be restarted' killings starting 16:08:00Z.

The change that started the incident was the in-place replacement of the checkout pod's container (and wait-for-kafka init) image with gcr.io/google-containers/pause:latest at ~16:08:00Z, which produced the crash loop, removed the only ready checkout endpoint, and therefore made frontend's CheckoutService/PlaceOrder client spans fail from ~16:08-16:09 onward. The pod's own image-override annotations (checkout-normal, wait-for-kafka-init) and the timing match, but the actor that performed the change is not observable in this Run.

Secondary candidate not confirmed as a cause: the checkout Deployment template defines no readinessProbe or livenessProbe for the checkout container, so pod readiness depends only on the container running; this did not cause the alert (the pause container crashes and the endpoint is notReady) but it weakens protection against a running-but-non-serving checkout container.

Restore the checkout pod so its container uses ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-checkout and its wait-for-kafka init uses busybox:latest (values recorded in the pod annotations and still present in the Deployment/ReplicaSet templates), e.g. by recreating the pod through the checkout ReplicaSet/Deployment, then confirm Deployment checkout reports READY=AVAILABLE=1 and the checkout Service endpoint has ready addresses again.

Add a readinessProbe (and livenessProbe) to the checkout container in the Deployment template so a running but non-serving container is kept out of the Service endpoints, and verify frontend's PlaceOrder error spans return to zero after recovery.

gaps: The alert's own PromQL expression, threshold and reported value (3.5) could not be read: list_prometheus_rules for rule_name=RequestErrorRate returned no_data, and my computed frontend error-span ratio at the alert instant was 0.455%, so the unit of the annotation value is unknown.

No error trace details are available for the incident: Jaeger data in this Run ended at ~2026-11-16T16:02:03Z (the frontend traces_search result was RESULT_TOO_LARGE with that source_end_at), and traces_search/traces_search_by_tags for frontend and checkout after 16:05-16:11 returned no_data, so the gRPC status/error message on the failing PlaceOrder calls is unknown; the error attribution rests on span-metric series.

Application-level exit output from the crash-looping checkout container instances was not retrievable (previous instance not found; the readable current stream ends 2026-11-16T15:54:09Z), so the exact message printed before exit code 2 is unknown.

rpc_client_duration_milliseconds_count had no samples in the window (no_data), so gRPC status codes on frontend's clients could not be inspected; kube_pod_container_info and http_server_request_duration_seconds_count also returned no_data for these series.

The change_history integration is not available in this Run, so who or what replaced the checkout pod's container images at ~16:08:00Z (and whether it was an intentional fault-injection experiment) cannot be established from evidence.

Frontend application logs in 16:05-16:22 returned no lines (0 lines read), so the frontend side of the failures could not be confirmed from log text; frontend health there rests on pod status and its error-free non-checkout span series.
next_steps: Inspect the checkout pod's mutation source (admission webhook, chaos/fault-injection controller, or manual edit) now that the pod carries the annotations checkout-normal and wait-for-kafka-init; change_history is not integrated, so a human must check the audit/deployment history around 2026-11-16T16:08:00Z.

Recreate/restore pod checkout-5dccddf8bb-9dn2q with the images recorded in its annotations and confirm Deployment checkout readiness and the checkout Service endpoints, then watch frontend's CheckoutService/PlaceOrder error spans clear.

Add readiness/liveness probes to the checkout container template and raise alert fidelity by checking the RequestErrorRate rule definition in the alerting backend (it is not loaded/visible in this Prometheus instance).
